items.text: OUT-001 and OUT-002 require local-first selection, explicit person choice plus supplied key for cloud use, and configured-server-only local traffic; OUT-003 includes allowed local, disallowed destination and cloud-choice/key-absence cases with their expected outcomes. Verification: VER-001. Sources: REQ-001 and its assigned source clauses.

verification.text: Trace model-selection and destination cases in OUT-002/003 to PRD V4-HOST-01/02 and Architecture V4-ARC-11. Inspect the expected local/cloud choice/key outcomes and evidence separation; later host execution observations must identify configuration and observed destinations. Record missing host observations explicitly.

items.text: OUT-001, OUT-002 and OUT-003 identify the host native network enforcement point and require keys to remain outside interface scripts; fixture evidence is labelled separately from actual native enforcement evidence. Verification: VER-002. Sources: REQ-001, CLM-001 and Architecture V4-ARC-12.

verification.text: Inspect the native-network receiving contract and endpoint/key cases against Architecture V4-ARC-12. Require evidence of the actual native routing/enforcement and script/key separation before claiming host conformance; model fixtures alone verify only the expressed receiving expectations.

items.text: OUT-001 and OUT-002 describe minimal Chat Completions tool-call capability and all four replaceable boundary subjects—messages, tools, events and checkpoints—while keeping App Codex interfaces separate, exact supplier/version/wire choices open and Pi unselected. Verification: VER-003. Sources: REQ-002 and Architecture V4-ARC-10/14.

verification.text: Review the loop contract and interface fixtures for all four replacement subjects and minimal Chat Completions tool calls; compare their interface identity to the distinct App Codex boundary and inspect the open supplier/version/wire choices and Pi exclusion against Architecture V4-ARC-10/14 and §§3/6.

items.text: OUT-001, OUT-002 and OUT-003 require catalog-schema validation before domain validation and include schema-invalid and schema-valid/domain-invalid cases; passing the first check does not bypass the second or constitute a human act. Verification: VER-004. Sources: REQ-003, Architecture V4-ARC-13 and Host V4-HI-20/25.

verification.text: Examine validation-order cases and, when supplied, host traces showing catalog-schema rejection before domain validation and schema-valid input proceeding to domain validation, which may reject it. Bind checks to adopted catalog identity and keep host application/human acts distinct.

items.text: OUT-001, OUT-002 and OUT-003 include truncated and malformed tool calls with expected reported failures and no empty-argument execution; a valid-call comparison distinguishes legitimate execution from rejected input. Verification: VER-005. Sources: REQ-003 and Architecture §4 failure property.

verification.text: Review and exercise conformance fixtures for malformed and truncated tool calls plus valid comparison calls; inspect failure reporting and absence of empty-argument dispatch for rejected input. Label fixture execution separately from received actual-host execution evidence.

items.text: OUT-001 and OUT-003 require a usable host interface during long parsing and model streaming, identify how actual host responsiveness will be observed, and avoid an invented latency limit or mandatory thread placement. Verification: VER-006. Sources: REQ-004 and Architecture §4 responsiveness property.

verification.text: Review the host responsiveness case definition for concurrent long parsing/streaming and interface interaction. Receive the host owner's candidate-bound observations of continued usability before claiming actual responsiveness; record environment, observations, implementation choice and limitations without inventing quantitative thresholds.

items.text: OUT-004 names the App/shared contribution, each excluded act's owner, required incoming contract meanings and external host evidence, and the OI-013/OI-014 decisions and points of need. Host internals stay with their owner, and common construction has no allocation absent a concrete agreed repeated responsibility. Verification: VER-007. Sources: REQ-005/006, CLM-001/002/003, Basis, Issues and Clarification.

verification.text: Independently compare the allocation/open-choice account to accepted Deliverables, Packages, OI-013/OI-014, DEP-001 and Clarification. Check excluded acts one-for-one against CLM-001/002/003; confirm required receiving work remains included and every proposed common construction identifies an agreed repeated responsibility before allocation.

items.text: OUT-001 and OUT-003 preserve separate event/evidence subjects for execution, proposal acceptance, checking, approval and professional reliance; cases reject success-as-acceptance and cross-act inference, retain the actual person as actor of reserved acts, and honor each declared checkpoint without fabricating a universal acceptance prerequisite. Verification: VER-008. Sources: REQ-007, CLM-004, Host human-act clauses and sealed brief distinct-acts clarification.

verification.text: Review checkpoint/event/evidence examples against adopted workflow, policy and record inputs. Check success-only, actual acceptance, independently evidenced checking, approval and reliance as distinct observations; reject cross-act inference and agent impersonation, and verify that a declared checkpoint awaits its own specified act.

items.text: OUT-003 and OUT-004 distinguish completed local contract checks from unresolved receiving inputs and absent actual-host evidence. Any later host conformance result identifies the received host candidate and observed evidence; an authored contract, fixture pass or owner-reported construction does not claim deployed behavior, adopted handoff, joined witness or product qualification. Verification: VER-009. Sources: Basis DEL-05-01 verification, Issues DEP-001, Clarification and Setup.

verification.text: Audit the conformance and owner account for exact source/candidate identity, actual observations and evidence gaps. Compare the claimed host standing to received DEP-001 material; require the host-specific evidence for any actual host claim and route any joined-journey claim to its owning examination contribution rather than infer it from this contract.
